chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad narrated from Abū al-Qāsim Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿĪṣ, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man dies while he is in a state of janābah. He said: “He is given ghusl for janābah, then afterward he is washed with the ghusl of the deceased.”

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: Major ritual impurity caused by janābah
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلَ: Ritual washing performed with a specific legal purpose
key_terms.يَمُوتُ: Dies; the ruling concerns the state at the time of death
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: He is washed; refers here to ritual washing

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a person dies while in a state of janābah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a deceased person who dies while in a state of janābah. It indicates that ghusl for janābah is performed first, and then the ghusl of the deceased is carried out afterward, showing the order of ritual purification in this case.
